lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Day one. You shoulder open the dispatch-center door — coffee in one hand, nerves in the other.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You've never taken a real call, just the academy sim. This place is louder, messier, and very, very caffeinated.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A corkboard crammed with schedules, sticky notes, and a couple of faded 'Have you seen me?' flyers nobody's taken down.

choices.label: Okay. How hard can it be?
Just don't crash on day one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Truth is, the city's a little jaded. People call 911 half-expecting no one to show. Your job: change their minds, one call at a time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Top of your console, a little bar: citizen trust. Right now it's barely a sliver.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You slip the headset on for the first time. The 'incoming call' light blinks. Here we go.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody starts an expert. Headset on. The 'incoming call' light blinks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gray morning. Your first shift's over. You climb the stairs of an old building that smells like reheated coffee.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: First full day. Did you eat anything in that place?

choices.label: There's a machine that dispenses coffee and regret.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Sit. I'll heat something up.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: I can tell. You carry it in your shoulders. Sit, I'll heat something up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She serves you without another question. Outside the city wakes up; in here, for a minute, nothing's wrong.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Always, kiddo. Now eat.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: I sleep when you get home in one piece. Eat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mid-shift. A call lights up. On the line, a worried voice — not panicked, just... off.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Hi, sorry. My brother never came home last night. That's not like him. And there was this van parked outside for hours.

choices.label: Okay, step by step. When did you last hear from him?
Can you give me your address?
Try not to worry yet. Tell me about the van.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She describes it: dark, no back windows, plates starting with a J. Probably nothing. Probably.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: It's probably silly. He's a grown man. I just... had a bad feeling. Please don't make a big deal of it.

choices.label: I'll send a patrol to take a quiet look around.
Let me log it and flag that plate, just in case.
I'm sure he'll turn up. Call back if not.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You log the plate and send a unit to circle the block. A small thing. You almost forget it... almost.

choices.label: I'll stay on the line while they check.
Call me back the second he shows up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The brother turns up by morning — shaken, vague about where he'd been. Loose end tied... mostly. Something about that van sticks with you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You move on to the next call. Hours later, a note lands: the brother's still not home. You jot the plate down anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Split screen: you at the console; on the other end, a kitchen vanishing into orange smoke.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: My kitchen is on fire! 🔥

choices.label: Are you out of the house?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: WHAT?! This is an EMERGENCY!

choices.label: And emergencies are what we do 😎
Sorry. Are you out of the house?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: No, it's way too hot!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I can't get out, it's too hot!

choices.label: Get out of the house NOW.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I need someone, please!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: 989 Burb Street.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sirens. The truck rounds the corner before the roof gives. The city breathes a little easier.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Citizen trust ticks up. Clean.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A patrol car at a house fire. The city notices, and not in a good way.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You let it burn. The city will feel that one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An anguished voice, echoing off bathroom tile. The camera, if there were one, would rather not come in.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: HELP! I'm out of toilet paper!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I don't care.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I'm barefoot!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Please, I pooped!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: So are you sending toilet paper?

choices.label: Yeah, I'll wipe for you too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nicely handled. Good judgment pays, and the city cracks a smile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A little too cheeky — but you filtered it. Counts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Call dropped. No pay, no problem.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A unit for toilet paper — tied up all afternoon, with the city watching.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in front of a screen of red, plunging charts. He dials a number he shouldn't.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I bought bitcoin and lost everything.

choices.label: Yikes. What are you gonna do?
Hey, chin up, it'll be okay.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I think I'll rob a bank.

choices.label: I'm going to have to send the police.
Can I come? I'm broke too.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: 80% for me, 20% for you?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I need therapy to get over this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Patrol on the way. Good call.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An 80/20 split with a suspect, straight from the console. The city does not forgive that one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You talked him down without spending a unit. That counts too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You talked him down fast. Nice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A dim alley. Something small shuffles between the trash cans. The caller is not breathing easy.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: I found a baby dinosaur!

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: That's what I thought too. Until now.

choices.label: Let's say I believe you… what breed?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: No, it's a baby! I think it's a T-REX. Maybe?

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: 18th, Jurassic St.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: 18th, Jurassic St.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Right unit for a weird one. That's how it's done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A patrol car versus a T-Rex? They'll bill you for that.
